# Month-end forecast range: method and SYNTHETIC results

**Every number on this page comes from SYNTHETIC months.** They were generated by
`ml/forecast/synth_months.py` on top of `ml/common/synth.py`; no real person's records were
used. They show how the method behaves on data with effects the rule does not assume. They are
not a measure of real-world accuracy, which needs at least three months of the owner's real
dated entries.

## What runs on the phone

The point forecast is the Phase 3 rule (`app/lib/domain/forecast.dart`), unchanged: spent so
far, plus the everyday daily rate (last 90 days, one-offs and regular payments taken out) times
the days left, plus the regular payments still due. Shown only after 7 days of entries.

The range around it (`ml/forecast/range.py`, ported to `app/lib/smart/forecast/forecast_range.dart`):

1. **Bootstrap.** 500 simulated months. Each draws one history day for the rest of today
   (only what is above what was already spent today, never below zero) and one history day for
   each day left, with replacement, and adds them up.
2. **Cut-offs.** The 10th and 90th percentiles of the 500 totals (an 80% range), by linear
   interpolation on the sorted totals: `h = (n - 1) * p`,
   `value = s[floor h] + (s[ceil h] - s[floor h]) * (h - floor h)`.
3. **Regular payments.** Low adds each due payment's low amount, high its high amount.
4. **Snapshot adjustment.** Each earlier month with a saved forecast gives one error,
   `(actual - snapshot point) / snapshot point`, from its snapshot taken nearest the same day of
   the month. With `k` such months (newest 12) and `w = k / (k + 3)`, with `lo` and `hi` the
   range's edges relative to the point:
   `lo' = lo + w * min(0, p10(errors) - lo)` and `hi' = hi + w * max(0, p90(errors) - hi)`.
   It only widens. Months with no snapshot give no adjustment.
5. **Clamp.** Low is at least the money already spent and at most the point; high is at least
   the point.

Rounding is `floor(x + 0.5)` in both languages.

### The fixed random numbers

The bootstrap must give the same numbers in Python and Dart, so it uses a written-out PRNG,
not the language's own:

```text
32-bit xorshift (Marsaglia 2003), shifts 13, 17, 5
seed:  state = (0x9E3779B9 XOR dayOfMonth) AND 0xFFFFFFFF; if state == 0 then 0x9E3779B9
next:  x ^= (x << 13) & 0xFFFFFFFF;  x ^= x >> 17;  x ^= (x << 5) & 0xFFFFFFFF
index: x mod n          (n = number of history days)
order: sample 0's rest-of-today draw, then its days-left draws, then sample 1, ...
first five states for day 1: 1359504952, 3827716927, 3866437631, 332804602, 1758100174
```

The constants are in `app/assets/smart/forecast_params.json` (written by `export.py`); a Dart
test checks they equal the Dart constants. The parity test
(`app/test/smart/forecast_parity_test.dart`) runs 20 SYNTHETIC input vectors and 4
snapshot-error vectors through Dart and requires Python's low, point and high exactly
(maximum difference 0) and the unrounded percentiles within 1e-9. Changing the seed constant in
Dart makes 15 of its 26 tests fail.

## The synthetic months

16 synthetic people, 17 calendar months each from 1 January 2025. The first three months are
history only; 222 months are evaluated (a person's last month is dropped when the generator's
days end inside it). On top of the base generator:

- **weekday pattern:** Monday to Wednesday x0.85, Thursday x0.9, Friday x1.15, Saturday x1.3 to
  x1.9 (per person), Sunday halfway between;
- **payday bursts:** up to 1 to 4 extra shopping, family or other entries on each of the 1st to
  3rd of the month;
- **heavy-tailed one-offs:** on 1.5% to 5% of days, a payment of 30,000 x Pareto(1.2), capped at
  5,000,000;
- the base generator's regular payments (rent, school term, gym, DStv, Netflix, insurance),
  with skipped months and date jitter.

## Backtest

On the morning of every day from the 8th to the month's end (entries up to yesterday known;
days with fewer than 7 entry days this month are skipped, as on the phone), make the forecast
and compare it with what the month really ended at. 5,157 forecasts. Run
`python -m forecast.backtest` from `ml/`; the full output is in `backtest_results.json`.

Baselines: **run-rate** (spent so far / days gone x days in the month, no range) and **last
month** (last month's total). The **Phase 3 range** (mean plus or minus one standard deviation
of daily spending times the square root of the days left, plus regular bands) is shown for
comparison, since it is what the app showed before this phase.

| SYNTHETIC | forecasts | MAPE point | MAPE run-rate | MAPE last month | coverage bootstrap | coverage bootstrap + snapshots | coverage Phase 3 range | width bootstrap | width + snapshots | width Phase 3 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| all days | 5157 | 9.7% | 17.6% | 22.2% | 70.1% | 74.6% | 60.9% | 25.5% | 28.5% | 20.3% |
| days 8-14 | 1511 | 13.7% | 32.2% | 22.3% | 67.8% | 72.2% | 55.5% | 35.1% | 39.1% | 27.7% |
| days 15-21 | 1554 | 10.8% | 17.0% | 22.3% | 69.8% | 74.7% | 59.3% | 28.3% | 32.3% | 22.4% |
| days 22-end | 2092 | 6.1% | 7.5% | 22.2% | 72.0% | 76.2% | 66.0% | 16.4% | 18.1% | 13.3% |

Coverage is the share of forecasts whose real month total fell inside the range (the target is
80%). Width is (high - low) / real total. 4,789 of the forecasts had at least one earlier
snapshot month; on those, coverage was 71.7% for the bootstrap alone and 76.5% with the
adjustment.

### Reading it

- On these synthetic months the point forecast's error (9.7%) is about half the run-rate's
  (17.6%) and well under last month's total (22.2%). Early in the month the run-rate is poor
  (32.2% on days 8 to 14) because payday bursts inflate the first days.
- The bootstrap range covers 70% of real totals, short of the 80% it aims at. It resamples days
  independently, so it misses the weekday pattern, the payday burst still to come next month
  and one-offs (which are left out of the rate but still happen). The Phase 3 range covered
  61%.
- The snapshot adjustment brings coverage to 74.6% overall (76.5% where a snapshot exists) for
  a range about 12% wider. It is still under 80%: with few months the 10th and 90th percentiles
  of the person's own errors are noisy and are only given part of the weight.
- **A design decision was made on this synthetic data.** The first adjustment rule blended the
  edges toward the errors' percentiles in both directions; it narrowed the range when there
  were only one or two months and cut coverage to 65.2%. It was replaced by the widen-only rule
  above. The shrink constant (3 months) was fixed before that comparison and changing it to 1
  or 0.5 moved coverage by less than one point. Because the choice was made on these months,
  the 74.6% is optimistic for them.

## Not shown, and why

- Nothing about real accuracy: there is no real data yet. "How close it has been" on the
  phone will report only the person's own saved forecasts against their own months.
- The range is still below its 80% target here. A month-of-year or weekday-aware bootstrap
  would likely help; it is not built, because the synthetic effects were chosen by us and
  tuning to them would overstate the gain.
